headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Strong momentum, but leverage keeps cooling

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The market is in an early-stage uptrend and signal confidence has stepped up to high (70/100), led by a strong one-month momentum picture. That supports increasing acquisition spend, weighted toward active-trader and non-stablecoin channels, while keeping some budget in reserve because the long-term average is still declining, only about half of recent days closed above it, and long-term interest rates remain high. This is a budget-posture view built on past data, not trading advice and not a forecast.

reasons: BTC is 19% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.19).
Funding further below normal (z -1.01) even with Fear & Greed at 67.
200-day average still falling (-4.4% over 90 days); breadth only 51%.
watch: The key tension is between strongly bullish momentum (+0.48) and leverage that keeps backing away: funding has dropped from z +0.79 to -1.01 over two days and sentiment has slid to a flat +0.02, while price has pushed higher and short positions, not longs, have been liquidated. That means the trailing price trend is advancing without a leveraged chase, with breadth still only 51% and the 200-day average still sloping down. Breadth moving clearly above 55% and the 200-day slope turning flat or positive would confirm the read; price slipping back toward the roughly $73,700 short-term-holder cost basis, or several sessions of ETF outflows, would weaken it.
analysis: Short-term sentiment is neutral (+0.02 of a possible ±1), slipping further from +0.11 yesterday and +0.445 two days ago, so the near-term mood signal has now cooled to almost exactly flat. The main reason is positioning rather than mood: the funding z-score fell again to -1.01 from -0.68, meaning perpetual longs are paying noticeably less than normal, which cuts against the Fear & Greed Index still sitting in Greed at 67 (down from 72). That gap is the defining feature of the week — the crowd describes itself as greedy, but leveraged traders are not paying up to express it. The long/short ratio rose back to 1.19 from 1.04 and open interest edged up to about $8.29B from $8.22B, a mild tilt toward longs that slightly pulls against the neutral read, though without the funding premium that usually accompanies a crowded trade. Cointelegraph reported about $210M of crypto liquidations over 24 hours on 2 October, including roughly $122M of BTC shorts as price pushed toward $87K, consistent with shorts rather than longs being forced out. Volatility measures sit on the calm side and add little directional weight: realised volatility is at the 41st percentile of its two-year range, Bollinger width is 16%, DVOL is 34.8 and the VIX is 15.3, while a stablecoin supply ratio of 5.46 points to a moderate pool of sidelined liquidity. The lean would turn bullish if funding moved back above normal alongside the greed reading, and bearish if Fear & Greed fell while open interest kept building on negative funding.

Medium-term momentum is strongly bullish (+0.48 of a possible ±1), up from +0.46 and the strongest of the three dimensions for a second day. Reinforcing that, the 90-day rate of change is +33%, weekly RSI is 59.8 — firm but well short of overbought — and the 50-day average is now 10.0% above the 200-day, widening the golden-cross spread. Participation is improving only slowly: 51% of the last 90 days closed above the 200-day average, up from 50%, which is the weakest part of the picture and the main thing cutting against the strong lean, since the headline 90-day gain rests on a relatively narrow share of strong days. Network and market-share data reinforce the lean, with active addresses 14% above their yearly average (from 11%) and BTC dominance at 58.7%, so activity is concentrated in bitcoin rather than rotating into altcoins. Flows have steadied after the 30 September outflow: Yahoo Finance reported spot bitcoin ETFs took in about $103M on Thursday 1 October, reversing the prior day's outflows, and the pipeline's latest daily ETF figure is a smaller net inflow of about $31.7M. The next FOMC meeting is on 27–28 October. The lean would firm further if breadth moved clearly above 55% with ETF inflows sustained, and weaken if weekly RSI rolled over or outflows resumed for several sessions.

The long-term trend is bullish-leaning (+0.26 of a possible ±1), essentially unchanged from yesterday and still an early, unconfirmed lean. Supporting it, price is about 19% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.19); cutting against it, that average is still falling, down 4.4% over 90 days, though the decline keeps flattening (from -4.6% yesterday and -4.9% the day before). That combination — price back above the trend line before the line itself turns up — is why trend trails momentum by a wide margin. Valuation is neutral for the lean: the 200-week multiple of 1.28 is mid-range, price is 32% below its all-time high, the Puell Multiple of 1.19 puts miner revenue in a normal band, and the Pi-Cycle gap of -55% is far from levels historically seen near cycle tops (context only, not scored). KuCoin News reported the short-term-holder cost basis at about $73,700 as of 1 October, so recent buyers are on average in profit, which supports the lean. Macro remains the clearest cross-current: the US 10-year yield is 5.28% against a fed funds rate of 3.63%, a substantial competing return for a non-yielding asset; Yahoo Finance reported a soft September payrolls print of 29,000 on 2 October, and on the structural side the SEC proposed a dedicated crypto custody framework for investment advisers, per Investing.com. Cumulative spot ETF net inflows of about $57.7B and roughly 1.28M BTC held by public companies reinforce the lean, which would strengthen if the 200-day slope turned positive and flip toward neutral if price fell back below that average or under the short-term-holder cost basis while long yields stayed this high.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels: a +33% 90-day move with the 50-day average 10% above the 200-day gives campaigns a concrete recovery story, and high signal confidence (70/100) supports a fuller push. Lead with the trend and the strengthening quarter-start rather than urgency — Fear & Greed is already at 67 while leverage is cooling (funding z -1.01), so FOMO angles would run ahead of the data; keep stablecoin-first channels at steady, not expanded, spend.
